cases.purpose: A non-root broadcaster gets EPERM for victims owned by another uid, still signals later victims it owns (status 0), reports each refusal on stderr, and exits 2 when no delivery succeeds.
cases.oracle: Trap logs of victims owned by uid 4242 and 4343 in a private PID namespace; kill(2) permission rule for a non-root broadcaster (uid 4343) and documented killall5 statuses 0/2.
cases.comparison: Candidate output, status and files compared with values derived independently of candidate output.

files.inner.sh:
tick() { read -t "$1" -u 7 || :; }
start() { /usr/bin/python3 victim.py "$@" & until [[ -s $1.ready ]]; do tick 0.05; done; }
exec 7<> wait.fifo
VICTIMS=(a b c d)
show() { local f L; for f in "${VICTIMS[@]}"; do L=(); [[ -e $f.log ]] && mapfile -t L < $f.log; local IFS=,; printf ' %s=%s' $f "${L[*]:--}"; done; echo; }
eperm() { local e n=0 line; e=$(< err.txt); while IFS= read -r line; do [[ $line == *"Operation not permitted"* ]] && n=$((n+1)); done <<<"$e"; REPLY=$n; }
# a and c belong to uid 4242, b and d to uid 4343 (the broadcaster); a has the lowest pid, so its EPERM comes first
start a session 4242; start b session 4343; PB=$!; start c session 4242; start d session 4343; PD=$!
bc() { /usr/bin/setpriv --reuid=4343 --regid=4343 --clear-groups "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c "$1" 2>err.txt; }
bc 'killall5 -USR1'; rc=$?
for i in {1..40}; do [[ -s b.log && -s d.log ]] && break; tick 0.05; done
tick 0.3
eperm; printf 'mixed-broadcast status=%s eperm-lines=%s' $rc $REPLY; show
: > b.log; : > d.log
# omit the two victims owned by the broadcaster: every remaining delivery is refused
bc "killall5 -USR1 -o $PB,$PD"; rc=$?
tick 0.3
eperm; printf 'all-foreign status=%s eperm-lines=%s' $rc $REPLY; show

cases.script:
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; os.mkfifo("wait.fifo")'

echo "ns status=$?"
cases.stdout:
mixed-broadcast status=0 eperm-lines=2 a=- b=USR1 c=- d=USR1
all-foreign status=2 eperm-lines=2 a=- b=- c=- d=-
ns status=0
